skill.name: enact-firecrawl
skill.description: Use Firecrawl to scrape, crawl, map, search, and extract website content as markdown or structured data.
skill.summary: Convert websites and web search results into markdown or structured data through the Firecrawl API.
skill.author: EnactProtocol

security_audit.summary: Static findings are mostly expected Firecrawl API use, credential handling, documentation examples, or a remote webpage screenshot feature. The main risks are unquoted input interpolation in the runtime command, third-party transfer of arbitrary URLs and prompts, and missing maximum limits for crawl or search scope.

remediation.issue: Runtime command interpolates user-controlled fields directly.
remediation.suggestion: Use an argv-style command form or pass parameters through JSON or stdin. Quote or escape values if a shell is unavoidable.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary URLs, queries, prompts, and schemas are sent to Firecrawl.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose this third-party transfer clearly. Add allowlists or confirmation for private domains, signed URLs, and sensitive prompts.

remediation.issue: Crawl and search limit values have no explicit maximum.
remediation.suggestion: Set a reasonable maximum in inputSchema and validate it in Python before calling Firecrawl.

remediation.issue: Screenshot format can capture full remote page images.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit opt-in for screenshot output and warn users before capturing private pages.

semantic_findings.title: Unquoted Input Interpolation in Runtime Command
semantic_findings.description: The runtime command interpolates action, URL, formats, limit, prompt, and schema values directly into one command string. If Enact executes this through a shell, crafted input could alter arguments or run unintended commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command field clearly embeds user-controlled variables without quoting. Confidence is not higher because exploitability depends on Enact runtime argument handling.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Data Transfer for Arbitrary URLs
semantic_findings.description: The skill accepts arbitrary URLs, search queries, prompts, and schemas, then forwards them to Firecrawl. Private links, signed URLs, or sensitive extraction instructions may leave the user environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The input schema accepts URLs or search queries, and the Python code sends those values to Firecrawl API requests. This is expected behavior but needs clear data-transfer controls.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Crawl and Search Scope
semantic_findings.description: The input limit has no explicit maximum in the schema or Python validation before calling Firecrawl. A large limit could increase cost, runtime, or unintended crawl scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The schema defines a default limit but no maximum, and the code passes the parsed integer to Firecrawl. API-side limits may reduce impact.

content.value_statement: Web research often needs clean page content, links, and structured fields. This skill uses Firecrawl to scrape, crawl, search, and extract data for AI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Scrapes a single URL and returns Firecrawl content in requested formats.
Crawls a site with a page limit and polls Firecrawl until completion.
Maps website URLs with an optional search filter.
Searches the web and returns scraped results from Firecrawl.
Extracts structured data from URLs using a prompt and optional JSON schema.
Requests remote webpage screenshots when screenshot is included in formats.
limitations: Requires a valid Firecrawl API key and outbound network access.
Sends target URLs, queries, prompts, and schemas to Firecrawl.
Does not enforce domain allowlists, robots policies, or crawl budgets itself.
Long crawl and extract jobs can time out during polling.

use_cases.title: Prepare Documentation for AI Search
use_cases.description: Crawl a documentation site and collect markdown pages for indexing, summarization, or retrieval workflows.

use_cases.title: Collect Research Sources
use_cases.description: Search the web and retrieve cleaned page content for comparison, notes, and citation review.

use_cases.title: Extract Market Data
use_cases.description: Pull pricing, product details, or public page fields into a consistent structured format.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect one page as markdown.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use enact-firecrawl to scrape [URL] as markdown. Return the main content and metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl a Small Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl [documentation URL] with action crawl and limit 5. Return page titles, URLs, and markdown summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Search Web Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic] with limit 5. Compare the returned pages and cite source URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Extract With a Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: return consistent fields from a page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract pricing plans from [URL]. Use my schema fields for plan name, price, billing period, and included features.

output_examples.input: Scrape a product page as markdown.
output_examples.output: Returns a success status, the source URL, cleaned markdown content, and page metadata.

output_examples.input: Crawl a documentation site with a limit of five pages.
output_examples.output: Returns discovered pages with URLs, titles, markdown content, and crawl status details.

output_examples.input: Extract the top headlines from a public news page.
output_examples.output: Returns structured headline details when Firecrawl can identify the requested fields.

best_practices: Start with small crawl limits before increasing scope.
Avoid private, signed, or sensitive URLs unless sharing with Firecrawl is approved.
Use focused extraction prompts and minimal schemas for reliable structured results.
anti_patterns: Running broad crawls against sites without permission or a clear purpose.
Passing secrets, personal data, or access tokens in URLs, prompts, or schemas.
Requesting screenshots or HTML when markdown is enough for the task.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It calls Firecrawl to scrape, crawl, map, search, and extract website data for AI workflows.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads FIRECRAWL_API_KEY from the environment and uses it for Firecrawl API requests.

faq.question: Can it process private websites?
faq.answer: It can receive any URL, but you should only send private URLs when approved to share them with Firecrawl.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Target URLs, search queries, extraction prompts, schemas, and requested page content are sent to Firecrawl.

faq.question: Does it execute code from scraped pages?
faq.answer: No evidence found that it executes page code locally. Firecrawl processes pages remotely through its API.

faq.question: How should I control cost and scope?
faq.answer: Use low crawl and search limits, narrow URLs, and focused extraction prompts.
